title: EU/EEA/Swiss Free Movement — Netherlands Registration
description: EU, EEA, and Swiss nationals exercise free movement rights and do not require an IND residence permit to live or work in the Netherlands. They must register at their local municipality (gemeente) within 4 months of arrival. Registration in the BRP (Basisregistratie Personen) results in automatic BSN assignment.

title: Highly Skilled Migrant (Kennismigrant) — Eligibility
description: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals may apply for a Highly Skilled Migrant residence permit if employed by an IND-recognised sponsor at or above the applicable salary threshold. The employer (recognised sponsor) submits the application. The permit is linked to the employment contract and is valid up to 5 years.

title: Highly Skilled Migrant — Salary Thresholds (2026)
description: The IND publishes annual salary thresholds for the kennismigrant route. For 2026: aged 30+: €5,942/month gross; under 30: €4,357/month gross; reduced rate (within 3 years of graduation or completing research): €3,122/month gross. Salary must also be market-rate for the role.

title: Highly Skilled Migrant — Application Process and Fees
description: The recognised sponsor submits the application (online via Business Portal or by post using Form 7511) and pays the application fee of €423. The IND must decide within 90 days. After approval, the applicant collects an MVV (entry visa) at the Dutch embassy/consulate within 3 months. The MVV is valid for 90 days. Upon entry, a VVR (residence permit card) is collected at an IND desk.

title: EU Blue Card — Eligibility
description: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals with a higher-education diploma (programme of at least 3 years), or 5 years of relevant experience at higher-education level (or 3 years for IT professionals within the last 7 years), may apply for an EU Blue Card. Employment contract must be at least 6 months. Employer must carry out economic activity and not have been fined in the past 5 years for listed labour violations.

title: EU Blue Card — Salary Thresholds (2026)
description: Standard rate: €5,942/month gross. Reduced criterion for recent graduates (within 3 years of completion): €4,754/month gross. These thresholds are published annually by the IND.

title: EU Blue Card — Application Process and Fees
description: Application fee: €423. Processing time: 30 days (recognised sponsor or simultaneous family application), 45 days (current permit holders for paid work), or 90 days (all others). Permit valid up to 5 years; valid until 3 months after employment contract ends.

title: Orientation Year (Zoekjaar) — Eligibility
description: For recent graduates/researchers who completed a degree or conducted scientific research within the past 3 years. Qualifying paths include: scientific research in NL, Erasmus Mundus joint master, accredited bachelor/master at Dutch institution, post-master (10+ months), or master/doctoral at top-200 foreign institution (ranked by at least 2 of Times Higher Education, QS, ShanghaiRanking). Cannot have previously held an orientation year permit for the same programme.

title: Orientation Year — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €254. IND must decide within 90 days. Permit valid for 1 year — cannot be extended. Work freely permitted without TWV during orientation year. Foreign degree holders from top-200 institutions must demonstrate English proficiency (IELTS 6.0 minimum or equivalent). After finding work, must transition to kennismigrant, startup, or self-employed permit.

title: Intra-Corporate Transferee (ICT) — Eligibility
description: For managers, specialists, or trainees being transferred by their employer to a Netherlands branch of the same company. Must have worked for the company abroad for at least 3 months. Transfer period must exceed 90 days. Salary must meet highly skilled migrant thresholds. Employment conditions must comply with Dutch law. Maximum transfer: 3 years (managers/specialists) or 1 year (trainees). NL branch must not have been set up solely to facilitate EU transfers.

title: ICT Permit — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €423. IND must decide within 90 days (may be extended). UWV advice period up to 5 weeks. MVV appointment within 3 months of approval. TB test required within 3 months of permit receipt. Recognised sponsors apply online; others by post.

title: Startup Permit — Eligibility
description: Applicant must play an active role (beyond shareholder/financier), be registered in the Chamber of Commerce, have an innovative business idea (new product/service/technology/method to the Netherlands), and possess a step-by-step business plan. Must have a RVO-listed facilitator who: has startup mentoring experience, is financially healthy, holds no majority interest in the startup, is not a close relative (within 3rd degree), and has an internal deputy.

title: Startup Permit — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €423. IND must decide within 90 days. Permit valid for 1 year maximum — cannot be extended; must transition to self-employed permit. MVV required within 3 months of decision. Income must be demonstrated via Dutch bank account or facilitator financing.

title: Researcher Permit (EU Directive 2016/801) — Eligibility
description: For non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals conducting research (paid, unpaid with grant, or doctoral) at an IND-recognised research institution. Must hold a higher-education degree providing access to doctoral programmes. Requires a valid employment contract or host agreement specifying research title, duration, funding, and start/end dates.

title: Researcher Permit — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €254 (paid by employer via direct debit). IND must decide within 60 days. Permit valid for contract duration up to 5 years maximum. Income threshold: €1,635.90/month without holiday allowance (2026 figure for researchers). Work permitted without restrictions. MVV and VVR issued together on positive decision.

title: Study Residence Permit — Eligibility
description: Non-EU/EEA/Swiss students at accredited (NVAO or EQAR) Dutch universities or HBO institutions. Educational institution must be an IND-recognised sponsor and submit the application. Applicant must be enrolled full-time, meet income/living cost requirements, and make sufficient academic progress (at least 50% of study credits per year).

title: Study Permit — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €254. IND must decide within 60 days. Institution submits application on behalf of student. MVV appointment within 3 months of decision. TB test required within 3 months of permit receipt. Student work allowance: up to 16 hours per week as employee, or full-time during June, July, August. Self-employed work permitted (no hour cap) with Chamber of Commerce registration. Foreign documents must be legalised and translated to Dutch, English, French, or German.

title: Partner/Spouse Residence Permit — Eligibility
description: For spouses, registered partners, or unmarried partners of a Dutch national or valid residence permit holder. Both parties must be 21+ (exception: if married before arrival to NL, then 18+). Relationship must be verifiable. Partners must be registered at same municipal address. Sponsor must meet income threshold (€2,337/month without holiday allowance for 2026). Partner must not pose danger to public order or national security.

title: Partner Permit — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €254. IND must decide within 90 days. MVV valid for 90 days after approval. Permit validity: 5 years (if sponsor is Dutch/permanent resident) or matches sponsor's permit expiration. Civic integration exam may be required abroad before MVV. TB test required on arrival. Antecedents Certificate (form 7601) required for partners over 12.

title: Minor Child Residence Permit — Eligibility
description: For children under 18 joining a parent in the Netherlands who holds Dutch nationality or a valid Dutch residence permit. Parent must have lived in NL for at least 1 year with valid permit (exceptions apply). Child must not be married/in partnership. Consent required from the other custodial parent if remaining abroad. Child must not pose threat to public order or national security.

title: Minor Child Permit — Application Process and Fees
description: Fee: €85. IND must decide within 90 days. MVV required — appointment at Dutch embassy/consulate within 3 months of decision. MVV valid for 90 days. Foreign documents must be legalised and translated to Dutch, English, French, or German.

title: MVV (Authorisation for Temporary Stay) — Process
description: The MVV is a long-stay entry visa issued at a Dutch embassy or consulate. It is required for most non-EU applicants before entering the Netherlands for stays exceeding 90 days. The IND grants MVV alongside the residence permit decision; applicant then makes an appointment at the relevant Dutch diplomatic post within 3 months. The MVV is valid for 90 days. Passport must be valid for at least 6 more months. EU nationals do not require an MVV.

title: IND Recognised Sponsor — Requirement
description: Employers, educational institutions, and research organisations must be registered as a recognised sponsor with the IND in order to apply for residence permits on behalf of highly skilled migrants, students, and researchers. A publicly searchable register is maintained by the IND and updated monthly. Cost of recognition: €5,080 (standard) or €2,539 (small business ≤50 persons or exchange purposes).

title: BRP Municipal Registration and BSN
description: All residents (EU and non-EU) must register in the BRP (Basisregistratie Personen) at their local municipality (gemeente). Registration triggers assignment of a BSN (Burgerservicenummer / Citizen Service Number), which is required for employment, banking, health insurance, and government services. EU citizens must register within 4 months of arrival. Non-EU permit holders typically register immediately after arrival.

title: Dutch Health Insurance (Zorgverzekering) — Obligation
description: Every person who lives or works in the Netherlands is legally obliged to take out standard health insurance (basisverzekering). Covers GP consultations, hospital treatment, and prescription medication. Insurers must accept any applicant for standard insurance and charge the same premium regardless of age or health. Children under 18 are covered without additional premium. Supplemental insurance is optional. A dedicated helpline (zorgverzekeringslijn.nl) exists for those coming from abroad.

title: DigiD — Digital Government Identity
description: DigiD is the Dutch government's digital identity system, enabling secure login to government services (tax authority, healthcare, municipalities). It requires a BSN for registration. Login methods include: DigiD app, SMS verification, username/password, or identity document scan. Available as a mobile app (iOS and Android).

title: Ukraine — Temporary Protection Directive (EU)
description: Ukrainians displaced by the conflict may be entitled to Temporary Protection under the EU Temporary Protection Directive. Under TP status in the Netherlands, holders may live and work without a separate IND work permit. TP status is reviewed and renewed periodically — current status should be verified at ind.nl/en/situation-ukraine. Ukrainians may also apply for regular IND permits (study, kennismigrant) if eligible.

title: Syria / Iran — Regular vs Asylum Routes
description: Syrian and Iranian nationals may use regular IND immigration routes (study permit, kennismigrant, researcher, etc.) if they have valid travel documents and meet standard eligibility criteria. Asylum/protection routes are separately handled by the IND asylum department. For professional/student personas, the regular permit routes documented in this knowledge base apply. For asylum-related information, refer to ind.nl/en/asylum.

title: UK Nationals Post-Brexit — Third Country Status
description: Since 1 January 2021, UK nationals are treated as third-country (non-EU) nationals in the Netherlands. They no longer benefit from EU free movement. UK nationals must apply for IND residence permits (kennismigrant, study, family, etc.) under the same rules as other non-EU nationals. MVV is required for stays exceeding 90 days.

title: Family Reunification — Income Thresholds (2026)
description: The sponsoring resident must demonstrate sufficient income for family reunification. 2026 thresholds: spouse/unmarried partner — €2,337/month (without holiday allowance) or €2,523.96 (with holiday allowance); single parent with child — €1,635.90/month (without holiday allowance) or €1,766.77 (with holiday allowance). Note: students sponsoring family face additional constraints — see study financing thresholds.
